text:
alex: thinking about a minimal compatibility shim for the /v3->/v4 migration — not a full proxy, just a lightweight query normalizer that fixes request shape differences for a subset of tenants. keeps runtime changes small. thoughts?
maria: short answer: yes if it avoids touching core runtime. main worry is streaming and content-negotiation edge cases.
sam: can you sketch where it lives? edge sidecar in front of gateway or a lambda-style transform on the gateway?
alex: proposal: tiny sidecar (Go) alongside the gateway service that: normalizes query params, coerces optional fields to canonical names, injects X-Compat-Mode header, and rewrites a couple legacy top-level fields into the new nested shape. lightweight, <1ms median extra.
lina: +1 to sidecar. please add a trace tag so we can filter perf/quality by shimged requests: trace.set_tag("shim", "query-normalizer") in the span.
maria: streaming still tricky. v4 sends chunked JSON frames with meta attributes; the shim mustn't buffer the stream and must pass-through framing. otherwise we break KV cache warmups.
alex: agreed. design: only operate on non-streaming endpoints or on requests with header Accept: application/json; for streaming requests the shim will only rewrite headers and auth, not payload.
sam: what about embedding requests where payload size matters? we shouldn't double-serialize. maybe do a header-based opt-in per-tenant: X-Compat-Query: normalize=true. default off.
alex: exactly. opt-in by tenant at first wave. rollout plan: wave 1 = opt-in tenants on staging, wave 2 = 5% prod traffic, wave 3 = 25%, wave 4 = global. canary window each wave for 2 hours.
lina: add metrics: shim.requests, shim.errors, shim.latency_ms P50/P95, shim.rewrites.count. also add a shim.telemetry tag to spans.
maria: operational concerns: who owns the code? infra or runtime? if infra owns, runtime team still needs a rollback path. we should make the sidecar feature-flagged and controlled via config in infra repo.
alex: infra owns the sidecar; runtime will maintain the compatibility matrix. I'll open an infra issue and assign leads. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/1234
sam: decided? sounds fine but we need an explicit test harness for streaming frames and for the KV cache heuristics. add e2e tests and a replay harness using recorded traffic.
alex: good call. action items: alex to draft RFC follow-up with code sketch + perf numbers, infra to prototype sidecar, runtime to provide a regression test plan. I'll drop PRs and link in the issue.
maria: one more: we should expose a header X-Compat-Trace: <reason> so product teams can tell why a request was normalized. helps debug.
lina: no objections. let's also add a migration dashboard tile showing % of traffic normalized and errors by tenant.
deploy-bot: Scheduled canary job for infra/sidecar prototype: staging deploy at 2024-05-21T19:00Z, prod canary slot reserved. :robot_face: 
alex: thanks everyone — I'll file the RFC follow-up and tag you. if no blockers by EOD tomorrow we'll spin up the prototype. :+1:
